svg.title: small-stalk event-driven architecture
svg.desc: Event-driven architecture for small-stalk: producer clients emit put-job events into the queue; mutation thread processes state changes asynchronously from a LinkedBlockingQueue; timer events publish timeout mutations; worker clients react by calling reserve, delete, and release. Producers and workers are fully decoupled.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does a producer client send a put command in small-stalk?')
g.text: Producer client A — put(job, priority, ttr)

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Can multiple producers enqueue jobs concurrently?')
g.text: Producer client B — put(job, priority, ttr)

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What timeout mutations do timers publish in small-stalk?')
sendPrompt('How does the LinkedBlockingQueue serialize state mutations in small-stalk?')
g.text: Serializes all state mutations — put · reserve · delete · release

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does the mutation thread do in small-stalk?')
g.text: Applies mutations to job state · updates ready / reserved / delayed queues

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What job states exist in small-stalk?')

g.text: Worker consumers — react to job events

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does a worker call reserve in small-stalk?')
sendPrompt('Can multiple workers compete to reserve jobs?')

svg.text: Producers only enqueue jobs · workers consume later through reserve — fully decoupled through mutation event channel
